1000833.etyen:
Inherited from Middle Norwegian Litlæ Hamar, attested in 1411, from Old Norse Litlihamarr, literally “little Hamar”. The Old Norse name is formed from litli (“little”) and the place name Hamarr (“Hamar”). An alternative Old Norse construction, Hamrinn litli (“the little Hamar”), is also attested.
Earlier Middle Norwegian documentary forms recorded by Oluf Rygh include Lilþlæ Hamars sokn (1359) and Lithlæ Hamars k. (1390), followed by Litlæ Hamar (1411), Litsla Hamar (1442) and Lislæ Hamars s. (1464). The modern spelling Lillehammer is first recorded by Rygh in 1578 and again in 1594. :contentR

1004417.etyen:
A fixed phrase consisting of det (“it”), var (“was”), så (“so”) and lite (“little”), literally “it was so little”. Used idiomatically to minimize the favour, gift or effort for which the speaker is being thanked.
Compare the parallel expressions Norwegian Nynorsk det var så lite (“it's nothing, you're welcome”), Swedish det var så lite (“you're welcome”) and Danish det var så lidt (“you're welcome”).

1004929.etyen:
From storfyrste (“grand prince”) + -lig (“adjective-forming suffix”), literally “grand-princely”.
The base storfyrste (“grand prince”) consists of stor (“great”) and fyrste (“prince”). The former is from Old Norse stórr (“big, great”), from Proto-Germanic *stōraz (“big, large”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂- (“to stand”). The latter is from Middle Low German vurste (“prince; first”), from Proto-Germanic *furistaz (“first, foremost”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *preh₂- (“before”).
Compare the parallel formations Danish storfyrstelig, Swedish storfurstlig, Dutch grootvorst
